sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Assembly of Bionic Companion Robotic Animals with Speech Synthesizers

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU bilateral investment treaty network concluded by the Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union with more than 90 counterpart states
Luxembourg double taxation agreement network comprising over 80 signed DTAAs (including Germany, France, Netherlands, USA, UAE, Singapore, Hong Kong and China)
EU internal market freedoms and EU free trade agreements with third-party states applicable through Luxembourg's EU membership
ICSID Convention and New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 19 December 2020; Luxembourg Commercial Companies Law of 10 August 1915 as amended; CSSF prudential circulars on AML/CFT; directly applicable EU and UN restrictive measures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of incorporation and approved articles of association of the SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary appointed by the founders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Luxembourg authentic public instrument; no Hague Apostille required for documents executed in Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of each subscribing shareholder and each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of each shareholder's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing state, or consular legalization by a Luxembourg embassy for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each shareholder and UBO, dated within three months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company, government tax authority or regulated bank in country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille through the competent national apostille authority, or consular legalization in non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or current trade-register extract for each corporate shareholder or corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry, chamber of commerce or equivalent commercial registrar of the corporate shareholder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the country-of-origin competent authority, alternatively consular legalization by Luxembourg diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney if any founder or UBO is represented before the Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary of the jurisdiction in which the power of attorney is granted
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the granting state, or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate or blocked-share-capital confirmation evidencing payment of the minimum EUR 12,000 share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg credit institution where the company in formation maintains its opening account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic bank certification; no apostille is required, but the bank certificate must be issued specifically for the incorporation file and endorsed to the notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based KYC before incorporation: identify every natural-person beneficial owner at or above 25%, and any person exercising control otherwise; verify identity and inspect the full corporate chain; screen all shareholders, legal representatives and UBOs against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, Interpol red-flag data, and domestic AML/PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates. The complete AML documentation file must be retained for five years after termination of the business relationship in accordance with the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via lbr.lu and the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL); incorporating filings are initiated through MyGuichet.lu with notarial authentication.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be coined in any language, but it must be representable in Latin characters; any non-Latin script requires a transliterated Latin version to be registered with the RCSL. Official RCSL filings and notarial deeds are in French, German or Luxembourgish as accepted by the registrar, with French being the standard for legal certainty. The name must be distinctive, lawful, non-offensive and not misleading as to the company's activities. If a name contains words from a foreign language, a certified translation of the exact meaning may be requested by the RCSL and included in the public file.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCSL rejects or raises a conflict on a proposed name, the applicant may, within 15 days of notification, file a written reconsideration with the RCSL through lbr.lu, attaching trademark clearance reports, registry extracts and the legal argument for distinctiveness. The RCSL may grant the name, issue a revised refusal or require amendments. A confirmed rejection may be appealed before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within two months of notification. The applicant may also immediately reserve a fallback name for a fresh 30-day reservation. A name reservation may be extended once for a further 30-day period upon written request before expiry; where an appeal is pending, the registrar may accept an extension as part of the appeal file.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or domiciled registered office is permissible if supplied by a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation and management company governed by the Law of 31 May 1999 on domiciliation companies. The provider must supply a physical Luxembourg address, accept service of notices, and maintain corporate records. For a low-risk, non-licensed commercial SARL selling AI pet robots over Stripe and credit-card rails, a virtual office is generally accepted for RCS registration, RBE filing and tax correspondence, but the company must maintain real substance indicators for Luxembourg corporate law and anti-abuse tests: a resident manager, local accounting records, adequate bank documentation, and an address where legal process can be served. A pure mail-box arrangement with no human activity could expose the SARL to the minimum-net-wealth-tax top-up under the Law of 21 December 2021 and to RCS/RBE deregistration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, estimated at 5-10%. Unannounced inspection is materially more common for regulated entities such as banks, asset managers and domiciliation companies than for an ordinary commercial SARL. Residual risk is mitigated by maintaining a live Luxembourg registered office and keeping minute books, UBO files and accounting records available at that address.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Minimum SARL share capital deposit into a Luxembourg blocked account in the name of the company in formation (EUR 12,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg credit institution chosen by the founders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum share capital under the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915; the amount remains a company asset and is not a public levy

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial drafting and execution of the incorporation deed and articles of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff applicable to share capital, with prevailing market fee of approximately EUR 800-1,200 for a standard single-shareholder SARL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL) / Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff of approximately EUR 75

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Official Journal of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg (Mémorial C / RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official publication tariff of approximately EUR 30, unless the notary includes publication within an all-inclusive fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial UBO declaration filing in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Nominal statutory electronic filing charge; in certain cases filing through the notarial authenticated RBE channel is free

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate counsel pre-incorporation due diligence, name clearance, UBO piercing, KYC/AML file preparation, drafting of shareholders' resolutions and coordination of apostille chain
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: fixed professional fee of EUR 1,500-2,500 for a low-risk private limited liability company with non-regulated robotic toy activity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization of founders' and corporate shareholders' origin documents (passports, addresses, good-standing certificates, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille and consular authorities in the shareholders' jurisdictions of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official government schedules; approximately USD 20-100 per document for five to eight documents plus courier fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of non-French corporate documents, personal identity documents and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market tariff of approximately EUR 25-50 per page plus notarial certification of conformity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed domiciliation / virtual office service for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Private negotiated market rate; typical EUR 500-1,000 for a low-volume commercial company with mailbox, physical address, and compliance oversight

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg corporate bank account opening, KYC verification and release-of-capital certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank published schedule; account opening, due diligence and certificate issuance generally EUR 150-450

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Code of Companies), Articles 309-1 to 360-1 (SARL provisions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif) and Articles of Association (Statuts) filed electronically with RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000 fully subscribed; at least 25% of each share's nominal value must be paid up upon subscription; payment confirmed by a bank certificate issued by a Luxembourg credit institution in the name of the company 'in formation'
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: the shareholders' subscriptions to the share capital, as set forth in the notarial deed of incorporation, are approved and confirmed. The registered office of the company is hereby established at [address in Luxembourg], and the board instructs the managers to execute all agreements and filings related to the registered office. The following natural persons are appointed as first managers of the company: [insert names]; each manager may act either jointly or severally in accordance with the articles of association. The board authorizes the managers to open bank accounts, file all declarations with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, register for tax and social security obligations, and pursue all necessary industrial and environmental permits. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Negative Certificate (Certificat de non-confusion)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on LBR's public database and submit an application for a negative certificate confirming that the proposed corporate name (e.g., 'Interactive AI Pet Robot SARL') is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company name. File the request via myguichet.lu or directly with the RCS desk.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and business purpose description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit alternative names or file an administrative appeal to the RCS within 15 days; reapply with a distinctive second choice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Capital Deposit and Blocking Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary 'company in formation' bank account in the name of the future SARL and deposit the minimum share capital of EUR 12,000. The bank will issue a certificate of blocked funds (attestation de blocage de fonds) confirming that each shareholder has subscribed and paid the required 25% minimum on each share. The certificate is delivered to the notary for use at the deed signing.
required_dossiers: Identity and proof of address of all shareholders and managers
Bank KYC forms and economic rationale
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises enhanced due diligence queries, provide additional documentary evidence (source of funds, business plan, references); if still delayed, open the account at another Luxembourg bank or request a notary-sponsored escrow solution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign a timed appointment with a Luxembourg notary. The notary reviews the draft statuts, verifies the negative certificate, capital blocking certificate, and the legal capacity of all signatories. The founders sign the notarial deed of incorporation, which contains the articles of association, registered office address, capital allocation, and first manager appointments.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of all shareholders and managers
Written consent of the registered office owner or lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies missing documentation, correct and resubmit the file; reschedule the signing; in case of substantive legal objections, revise the statuts with legal counsel and present again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Filing and Publication in the Official Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarial execution, the notary transmits the deed to the RCS for electronic filing. The RCS checks compliance, assigns the business registration number (numéro de matricule), and arranges publication of an extract in the electronic official gazette (Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations – RESA). Once published, the company has legal personality.
required_dossiers: List of directors/managers and their consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or refusal, request a formal statement of deficiencies; rectify within the given deadline (usually 15 days) and resubmit; or file a judicial appeal before the District Court of Luxembourg if the refusal is deemed unfounded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Corporate Governance Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office / board of managers of the SARL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, adopt the pro-forma resolutions, approve the registered office adoption, appoint officers, and delegate powers required for banking, tax, licensing, and regulatory filings. The meeting minutes should be signed and filed in the corporate records. Adopt internal governance rules and ensure compliance with the law.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed and RCS registration certificate
Draft minutes of first board meeting
Powers of attorney or authorizations for each manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a manager is unable to attend, use a proxy or hold a written resolution signed by all managers. If corporate records are incomplete, prepare and backdate correction resolutions in accordance with Luxembourg law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Environmental Operating Permit Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Environnement (EA) and local commune (municipality)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for an 'établissement classé' operating permit for the toy assembly / robotic pet manufacturing facility under the Law of 10 June 1999 on licensed establishments. The facility will be classified and subject to environmental/industrial conditions. The administrative file includes a technical description, site plan, waste and emissions data, fire safety measures, and EIA classification.
required_dossiers: Site plan and detailed technical description of manufacturing processes
Description of raw materials, chemicals, and waste streams
EIA classification notice or screening document
Fire safety and building code documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is refused or conditioned, the company may submit observations or apply for a modification within the administrative review period. An appeal may be lodged with the Administrative Tribunal within 40 days following notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry; Administration de l'Environnement – Direction des Autorisations et Déchets
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licensed Establishment Permit (Autorisation d'exploitation d'établissement classé)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement – Département des évaluations environnementales
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EIA Registration (notice) – Category 3 under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 9 January 2019; no full EIA report required for small-scale toy assembly operations, but environmental registration and compliance is mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with the Luxembourg Water Management Law of 19 December 2008 (abnormal pollutant concentration limits as set by the permit); VOC emissions to meet thresholds under Directive 2010/75/EU and Luxembourg air emission standards; hazardous waste handling must align with the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; electronic components subject to EU RoHS and WEEE directives.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the communal authority after an inspection by the Luxembourg Fire and Rescue Corps; structural load and building code acceptance by the commune; occupational safety and health clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) under the Labour Code, including workplace inspection, emergency planning, and equipment safety certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – Luxembourg indirect tax authority; portal: MyGuichet.lu (single access point) and AEDT e-filing systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must (1) register with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) to obtain a corporate identification number (Numéro d'immatriculation); (2) file standard VAT registration request (Form 645) with AEDT, either directly or through a fiscal representative if no establishment in Luxembourg; (3) provide constitutive documents, proof of economic presence or intended activity, and valid board resolution; (4) receive the Luxembourg VAT identification number (Numéro de TVA LU). The number is issued within 7–15 business days on submission of a complete dossier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Luxembourg SARL is fully tax resident and subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax on worldwide income subject to specific territorial exemptions (e.g., participation exemption).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid entity election exists in Luxembourg. Available elections include VAT grouping (assujetti unique) for VAT consolidation; option to apply standard VAT to otherwise exempt real-estate transactions; simplified small-business VAT scheme for turnover below EUR 30,000; and the option to apply the Luxembourg corporate income tax group contribution regime (subject to statutory form and economic substance conditions).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual turnover exemption for small enterprises established in Luxembourg; non-resident suppliers have no threshold and must register for VAT upon the first taxable supply in Luxembourg, unless covered by an EU VAT One-Stop-Shop special regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, SAP, or digital stamping mandate for standard B2B/B2C invoices. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies through PEPPOL (factur-x/UBL). B2B e-invoicing is permitted and legally equivalent to paper, requiring only authenticity of origin and integrity of content; no prior government authorisation or API clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported to a destination outside the European Union are zero-rated, provided the exporter retains documentary evidence of physical departure within a reasonable period. Related services to the exported goods (where the services directly benefit the goods being exported) and certain offshore B2B services supplied to non-EU customers are also zero-rated if effectively used and enjoyed outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Discharge EAD with customs stamp)
Bill of Lading (or CMR, Airway Bill, or other international transport document)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing foreign currency proceeds
Commercial Invoice and Intrastat/Extrastat declaration if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT law imposes export substantiation requirements that are actively audited. Where a zero-rating claim is disallowed, the entire VAT becomes due from the date of supply; interest at the statutory rate (currently 3% per annum above EURIBOR) applies. Intentional fraud is punishable by fines of up to EUR 50,000 or imprisonment and, in serious cases, aggravated penalties. Retrospective clawbacks may cover a 10-year limitation period in the case of fraud, and the exporter loses the right to deduct input VAT on the exported goods; criminal prosecution may follow.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Luxembourg (Banque centrale du Luxembourg – BCL), operating within the Eurosystem; banking and AML/CFT conduct supervision for credit institutions and electronic money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full capital- and current-account convertibility under EU law and the eurosystem framework; no exchange-control authorisation is required for inflows, outflows, dividends, or liquidation proceeds. The euro is legal tender and unrestricted in cross-border payments. Profit remittance through dividend distributions is legally unrestricted but is generally subject to Luxembourg dividend withholding tax at the domestic rate of 15%, reducible or exempt under tax treaties, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, or the Luxembourg participation exemption regime. Foreign-currency bank accounts are permissible, and no prior central-bank approval is required for capital injections or repatriations, provided the underlying corporate, substance, AML/KYC, and tax reporting obligations are satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement and no statutory mandatory conversion timeline or ratio. Exporters may retain receivables in EUR or foreign currency, convert freely, and settle trade payables as commercially required. Cross-border receipts are reported to the BCL/eurosystem for balance-of-payments and international-transactions statistics, normally by the resident bank rather than the exporter. Exporters should retain underlying sale contracts, invoices, transport documents, and payment confirmations to support AML source-of-funds reviews and any CSSF-required transparency in banking relationships.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium (supplementary rail only). Luxembourg permits payment services and e-money under the CSSF licensing regime implementing PSD2; an EU/EEA-licensed EMI may passport into Luxembourg, while a non-EU offshore EMI cannot operate a payment account or provide regulated cross-border payment services without a Luxembourg/EU licence or an authorised branch. A regulated EMI or global payment facilitator such as Stripe may be used for merchant credit-card collection, marketplace payouts, and small-value international disbursements, but the primary corporate treasury account should be held with a Luxembourg-licensed credit institution to ensure eurosystem clearing access, deposit protection, stable correspondent banking, and direct BCL statistical reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not require a director to appear physically at a bank branch as an absolute statutory condition, because the AML/KYC rules impose risk-based customer due diligence requiring reliable and independent verification of identity. In practice, most first-time corporate clients of Luxembourg banks will be expected to complete an in-person or verified video KYC interview; authorised signatories and beneficial owners may be required to attend a branch, a Luxembourg notary, or a Luxembourg embassy/consulate for identity verification. Remote opening is technically possible when documentation is notarised/apostilled, the ultimate beneficial owner structure is transparent, and a recognised video-identification solution is accepted by the bank, but account activation can be materially accelerated by a physical onboarding visit. Budget for at least one director or authorised representative to attend bank meetings in Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership or multi-tier cross-border group structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO declaration filed in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), current Luxembourg trade register excerpt (RCS), notarised articles of association, full group organisation chart, shareholder registry, share-transfer chain documentation, sworn English translations, and a legal cover letter explaining the 100% ownership path from each UBO to LU_SARL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds or source-of-wealth mismatch in the inbound capital subscription
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed board resolution approving the capital injection, share subscription agreement, 3-6 months bank statements of the contributing shareholder or parent, source-of-wealth statement, tax residence certificates, audited or management financial statements of the parent, evidence of the corporate commercial activity, and a reconciliation of the exact capital amount against bank MT103 payment instructions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATCA/CRS classification ambiguity or doubtful tax residence of shareholders/directors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Form W-8BEN/W-8BEN-E or CRS self-certification for every reportable controlling person, Luxembourg tax-residence certificate for LU_SARL, proof of Luxembourg substance (office lease, local director or employee arrangements, bank account, operational contracts), and written confirmation that no treaty-shopping structure is present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Positive sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media screening hit on a shareholder or counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport copies, sanctions and PEP questionnaire, explanatory statement addressing any name matches, official public-registry extracts, independent third-party due-diligence report, negative-news search, legal opinion confirming no sanctioned connection, and evidence of the legitimate commercial purpose of the transaction or relationship.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the share-capital contribution from the offshore or EU parent by SWIFT MT103 in EUR to the Luxembourg operational bank account. Field 59 must state the exact LU_SARL legal name and IBAN; Field 70 should read 'SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / LU_SARL' and, where the receiving bank requires an ISO 20022 purpose code, use 'EQUI' (equity) or 'CAPH' (capital increase) as accepted by the beneficiary bank. Field 71A should be set to 'OUR' so that the full amount reaches the SARL without correspondent deduction. Deliver to the bank outside the remote system a complete equity-issuance dossier: signed shareholder resolution, subscription deed, updated RCS excerpt, UBO declaration, source-of-funds evidence, tax self-certifications, and an economic-substance summary. No exchange-control permit is required; the receiving Luxembourg bank will classify the inbound amount as direct investment and report it to the BCL/eurosystem for balance-of-payments statistical purposes. Do not route capital through personal accounts, third-party pass-through accounts, or unregulated fintech intermediaries.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments within the SEPA zone, including component purchases and EU supplier settlements. For non-EUR payments outside the eurozone, use SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary name, IBAN/account number, SWIFT/BIC, invoice references, and transfer-purpose details; set correspondent charges to 'OUR' or allocate charges under 'SHA' only when commercially agreed. For documentary trade settlements, use a Commercial Letter of Credit opened via MT700 and amendments via MT707, governed by ICC UCP600, with the bank's trade desk confirming documents against the credit. Maintain a complete trade file for each disbursement: purchase order, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading/CMR/air waybill, insurance certificate, EORI/customs declarations (where goods cross borders), and inspection certificates. Intrastat/EXTRASTAT declarations must be made where value or volume thresholds are exceeded for intra-EU or extra-EU goods flows. Stripe and credit-card merchant settlements should be collected separately into the operational account and reconciled against processor fees, chargebacks, and settlement currency conversions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts on liquid pairs (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/JPY) for committed forecast trade exposures, generally up to 12 months and documented under an ISDA or bank master FX agreement.

Non-deliverable FX forwards (NDFs) for currencies with restricted onshore deliverability or limited liquidity, such as CNH/CNY, INR, KRW, or other offshore-accessible currencies, subject to bank appetite, board FX-policy approval, and EMIR margining requirements, where applicable.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR vs. foreign currency) for medium-to-long-term balance-sheet hedging of intercompany loans, shareholder advances, or acquisition financing, with appropriate credit-support annexes and clearing/valuation under EMIR.

Vanilla FX options or zero-premium collar structures purchased from a licensed investment firm or credit institution, used only to hedge underlying commercial exposure and not for speculative purposes, with CSSF suitability assessment and board-approved delegated hedging limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of SARL shareholders and approval of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record; minutes kept in the statutory minute book (no RCS filing for the AGM itself)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year end (e.g., 30 June following a 31 December year end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be held liable to the company for damages; shareholders may petition the court to convene a meeting; repeat defaults support a finding of managerial misconduct.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (comptes annuels / liasse fiscale) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year end (e.g., 31 July following a 31 December year end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is a criminal offence for directors: court fines of EUR 500 to EUR 5,000 per director; persistent non-filing is an official trigger for administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) of the SARL from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership information (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March following each calendar year; any change in shareholding or beneficial owner details must be reported within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false declaration is a criminal offence under the Law of 13 January 2019: fines of EUR 125 to EUR 1,250 for simple omissions and up to EUR 1,250,000 for knowingly false data; RBE may issue formal enforcement notices.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) including municipal business tax and net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL, the return must be filed by 31 December of the year following the taxable year (e.g., 2025 return due 31 December 2026); extensions may be granted via eSpace/MyGuichet
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Taxation d'office (estimated assessment), default interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax, late-filing fines up to EUR 4,000, and criminal prosecution for deliberate evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minimum net wealth tax payment (impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); filed together with the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the CIT return, due 31 December of the year following the tax year; minimum EUR 500 for a small SARL not holding over EUR 350k financial assets
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid minimum NWT attracts default interest at 0.6% per month and enforced tax collection; continued default may lead to enforcement measures against the company's assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit under Luxembourg law when a SARL exceeds two of the three thresholds for two consecutive years: balance sheet total over EUR 4.4 million; net turnover over EUR 8.8 million; average workforce over 50 employees. A 10% shareholder may request a specific audit even below thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified by the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts and EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS-EU is required for listed companies and optional for unlisted entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file an annual confirmation of its beneficial owners with the RBE before 31 March each calendar year. Share transfers or any change in control changing direct or indirect ownership above 10% require an RBE update within 30 days; the company must also retain an internal register and supporting corporate resolutions at its registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shares (Registre des actions nominatives)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 20,000 (only required if audit thresholds are exceeded; below thresholds, nil)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate in Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT = 1.19% + 6.75% municipal business tax); municipal business tax varies by commune
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box: 80% exemption of net qualifying IP income (software and patents embedded in AI pet robots), yielding an effective rate of approx. 5%; Notional Interest Deduction on eligible new equity; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (≥10% or ≥EUR 1.2M acquisition cost; 12-month holding); R&D tax credit up to 10% on qualifying R&D expenditure; investment tax credit for tangible fixed assets
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry; annual utilisation limited to EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess taxable base)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 807 (annual corporate income tax and municipal business tax return); filed electronically via the eCDF / MyGuichet.lu secured taxpayer portal; net wealth tax reported on Form 808
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; provisional quarterly CIT instalments paid in advance
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end (extensions available on justified request)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, RCS number, address, legal form (SARL), fiscal year start/end dates, business code NACE 32.40
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List Luxembourg registration details and appoint a tax agent; non-resident directors with no permanent establishment need no separate LU registration beyond the company file

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and profit/loss account (LUX GAAP or IFRS), accounting result before adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File the audited statutory accounts in the RCS as attached to the return; for foreign-parenthybrid instruments attach reconciliation schedules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reintegrations (non-deductible expenses, excessive interest) and deductions (participation-exempt dividends, IP box deduction, NID)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border recharges must be supported by an intercompany agreement and TP file; unsubstantiated management fees are recharacterised as hidden distributions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses brought forward and current-year taxable base after cap
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ownership changes >50% may forfeit carryforward; document the business purpose of any share transfer

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base, 17% CIT, 7% solidarity surcharge, and allocable tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require treaty TRC and proof of foreign tax paid; uncredited foreign income is separately reported

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax base and communal coefficient of the registered office commune
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax is assessed at the place of the Luxembourg permanent establishment; maintain payroll and premises substance to avoid relocation disputes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying shareholdings: 10% threshold or EUR 1.2M cost, 12-month holding condition, dividend and capital-gain exemption schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For foreign subsidiaries, attach TRC and proof of the 12-month holding intent to sustain the exemption

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying IP assets, nexus-ratio computation, 80% income exemption, and effective 5% rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: R&D must show economic substance in Luxembourg; licence-in and cost-sharing arrangements trigger the nexus ratio and substance audit risk

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: coercive fine (astreinte) of up to EUR 250 per contravention and a potential 10% late-filing surcharge on the assessed tax; late payment: statutory interest of 0.6% per month (7.2% p.a.); fraudulent non-filing triggers criminal fines of up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years, with publication of the sanction

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory rate; reduced to 0% under the Luxembourg participation exemption / EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for shareholders holding ≥10% for ≥12 months; treaty rates generally 5% (≥10% participation) or 15% (portfolio)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Recipient must obtain a certificate of tax residence (TRC) from its jurisdiction, complete Luxembourg Form 871 (or the equivalent refund application) and file it with the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) either to obtain exemption at source or to claim a refund; the TRC must evidence the proportionate participation threshold and holding period; standard refund claims are time-barred after five years from the end of the year of distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% domestic WHT on outbound royalties and interest (no Luxembourg withholding tax on interest or IP royalties); EU Interest & Royalties Directive and most DTAs also provide 0%, subject to beneficial ownership substance; exceptions for profit-distributing interest recharacterised as hidden dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: related-party transactions in excess of EUR 1,000,000 per transaction category (per ACD Circular L.I.R. 164/2); Master File: groups with consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 750,000,000; CbCR: groups with consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 750,000,000; documentation must be produced within 30 days of ACD request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No separate ESR statute; substance is enforced through Art. 56 LIR (sham transactions), Art. 164 LIR (arm's length), EU ATAD GAAR and CFC rules, EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive rules, and treaty beneficial-ownership requirements under the OECD MLI; a SARL manufacturing/packaging AI pet robots must maintain real premises, qualified staff, strategic decision-making in Luxembourg, and adequate capitalisation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission of Luxembourg-source profits, false declarations, or use of fictitious invoicing from shell foreign suppliers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to EUR 25,000 per offence, imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years, plus 100% surcharge on evaded tax and interest at 0.6% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may be criminally prosecuted, subjected to travel bans, and held civilly liable for the company's unpaid taxes under the fraudulent-acts doctrine (action en responsabilité, Art. 1382 Civil Code).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Letter-box SARL with no active management, no premises, no staff, and booking intercompany commissions to low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under Art. 56 LIR, denial of treaty benefits and IP box/NID relief, re-pricing under Art. 164 LIR, and assessment of hidden profit distributions with 15% WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Liability to third parties and the tax administration for gross negligence; exclusion from tax relief and, in cross-border fraud, personal extradition and asset-freezing orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash payments ≥ EUR 10,000 for AI pet robots without customer due diligence and failing to report suspicious transactions to the KYC/AML authorities (though credit card payment rails materially reduce exposure).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1,250,000 or 10% of annual turnover for serious AML breaches; criminal sanctions for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal prosecution, director disqualification, and personal civil liability for losses caused by AML breaches.
